answer: Minted twin keys fail a one-time harbor coupon test. Applicant locks 15.3 POA and draws berth pass BP-664 at shed H-8. Within 36 minutes they file a 0.74 kg copper coupon to 2.1 mm at bench M-5, hang it from cleat CL-12 at the south jetty so meter CT-3 logs 0.31 ohm after 90 s in 12 C water, then brush a 40 g umber patch on pile P-7 and photograph chip WC-18. Three non-kin clerks reweigh the coupon and match the pigment. A reused pass, resistance off by 0.04 ohm, or a dry pile keeps 6.2 POA and parks the key six epochs; 9.1 POA returns only after a later pass whose cleat and pile both change.
